cohort: The observational study included 1,316 individuals aged 20-59 from the National Health and Nutrition Examination Survey (NHANES) 2013-2016, while Mendelian randomization analysis used genetic data from 450,243 to 462,933 individuals.
finding: A significant positive correlation and a potential causal relationship were identified where sarcopenia susceptibility is associated with an increased likelihood of cesarean section, but no reverse causal link was found.
mod_finding: The number of cesarean sections was positively correlated with sarcopenia, whereas no such association was observed with vaginal delivery.
